title: BETWEEN LAB 1 AND LAB 2 — HOUR 2 QUICK CHECKS
instructions: Poll first, reveal answer second, ask a student to justify third.

questions.question: Which of these is a REGRESSION problem?
questions.explanation: Temperature is continuous. Spam and digits are classification; grouping news is unsupervised.

questions.question: In ŷ = β₀ + β₁x, the coefficient β₁ represents…

options.B: The change in ŷ per one-unit change in x

questions.correct_answer: The change in ŷ per one-unit change in x
questions.explanation: β₁ is the slope — the change in predicted outcome for a one-unit increase in x.

questions.question: In a multiple regression model, what is the best interpretation of coefficient β₁ = 2.0?

options.A: Increasing x₁ causes the outcome to rise by exactly 2.0
options.B: Holding other included features fixed, a one-unit increase in x₁ is associated with a 2.0-unit increase in predicted outcome
options.C: x₁ explains exactly 2% of the target variance
options.D: x₁ is twice as important as every other feature

questions.correct_answer: Holding other included features fixed, a one-unit increase in x₁ is associated with a 2.0-unit increase in predicted outcome
questions.explanation: Multiple-regression coefficients are conditional on the other included features. It is an association, not automatically causal.

questions.question: Multiple linear regression differs from simple linear regression in that it:

options.B: Uses two or more input features

questions.correct_answer: Uses two or more input features
questions.explanation: Simple linear regression uses one feature; multiple linear regression uses two or more.

questions.question: Polynomial regression is still considered a 'linear' model because:

options.A: It always draws a straight line
options.B: It is linear in its coefficients (parameters)
options.C: It only works on straight-line data

questions.correct_answer: It is linear in its coefficients (parameters)
questions.explanation: 'Linear' refers to the parameters, not the shape of the curve. The β coefficients appear to the first power.

questions.question: How should polynomial degree be selected?

options.A: Choose the degree with the lowest training error
options.B: Always use the highest degree available
options.C: Compare degrees using validation performance or cross-validation
options.D: Choose the degree that produces the smoothest-looking graph

questions.correct_answer: Compare degrees using validation performance or cross-validation
questions.explanation: Training error almost always improves with more flexibility. Generalization is judged on validation/CV data.

questions.question: Why does MSE penalize large errors more strongly than small errors?

options.A: Every residual receives the same penalty
options.B: Residuals are squared before being averaged

questions.correct_answer: Residuals are squared before being averaged
questions.explanation: Squaring gives large residuals disproportionately larger penalties, which is why MSE and RMSE are sensitive to outliers.

questions.question: Logistic regression outputs probabilities via which function?
questions.explanation: The sigmoid maps any real-valued score to a probability between 0 and 1.

questions.question: A logistic-regression model outputs P(y=1|x) = 0.72. Using a threshold of 0.50, what is the predicted class?

options.A: Class 0, because logistic regression cannot output probabilities

questions.explanation: 0.72 exceeds the threshold, so the predicted class is 1.

questions.question: What often happens when a binary-classification threshold is lowered from 0.50 to 0.30?

options.A: The model predicts fewer positive cases
options.B: Recall often increases, while precision may decrease
options.D: The model must be retrained before predictions can be made

questions.correct_answer: Recall often increases, while precision may decrease
questions.explanation: Lower thresholds flag more cases as positive — catching more true positives but also more false positives.

questions.question: With 98% negative samples, the most MISLEADING metric is…
questions.explanation: A model that predicts 'negative' for everyone scores 98% accuracy while finding zero positives.

questions.question: Which formula defines precision?
questions.explanation: Precision = true positives divided by all predicted positives (TP + FP).
